note: Per-pool fitted cut on lendingclub: is binary gating wrong, or was the cut wrong?
predicted: R78 showed the fixed EPV cut of 10 is actively harmful on MIMIC-IV (-40) and ACS TravelTime (-46), because the sign flips near EPV 5 there rather than 10. This asks whether binary gating is wrong or our CUT was wrong, with two new arms: gate_loso fits the cut on other target sites and applies it to the held-out one (deployable, same protocol as every other fitted rule here); gate_bestcut is the best single cut on the pool itself (in-sample, an upper bound on any single-threshold gate). MIMIC-IV smoke test: epv_gate -40, gate_loso 0, gate_bestcut +30, blend +30. PREDICTION: (1) gate_loso removes the negatives -- no pool below about -5 -- but does NOT reach blend, because a cut fitted to maximise mean AUPRC across sites is systematically too conservative where harm dominates; (2) gate_bestcut comes close to blend on most pools, so binary gating is achievable IN PRINCIPLE but not FITTABLE. FALSIFIABLE: if gate_loso matches blend, the paper should recommend a per-federation fitted gate and the continuous framing loses its main advantage.
